children: backed AI infrastructure startup Firmus Technologies is in talks to raise about $10B in financing ahead of its planned Australian IPO,
reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

The company is looking to raise about $7.5B in debt, split between senior and mezzanine portions, along with about $2.5B in equity. The debt facility could have a five-year tenor. The senior debt could carry an interest margin of around 275 basis points over the SOFR, while the mezzanine portion could carry about 725 bps over SOFR, the report said.

If completed, the financing would rank among the region’s largest digital infrastructure deals. Like a recent financing for Nvidia-backed Indonesian AI platform Zankore, Firmus’ proposed deal would include revenue sharing and credit support from Nvidia, according to the people.

Firmus’ financing talks come ahead of a planned IPO in late October that could raise up to $5B. The IPO proceeds would fund purchases of GPUs for the company’s 360-megawatt Nvidia DSX AI Factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which is being developed with DayOne Data Centers under an eight-year partnership with Nvidia
The proposed financing would add to Firmus’ existing funding. In February, the company secured a $10B loan from a consortium that included Blackstone
to accelerate its data center rollout in Australia. Six months later, investors, including Jane Street, committed $2B in equity.
Firmus began as a Bitcoin miner in Tasmania in 2019 and now operates seven AI factories across Australia, Singapore, Indonesia, and Malaysia.

title: Nvidia-backed Firmus plans to raise $10B before Australian listing - report
